title: What does Wythenshawe mean to the people who know it best?

evidence_packet.title: What does Wythenshawe mean to the people who know it best?
evidence_packet.lead: As Wythenshawe marks its centenary, 100 people tell the BBC what it is really like to live and work there
evidence_packet.summary: As Wythenshawe marks its centenary, 100 people tell the BBC what it is really like to live and work there
evidence_packet.evidence_text: This year marks 100 years since Wythenshawe Hall was donated to Manchester Corporation At the time, the city was in urgent need of more housing In 1920 an urban planner called Patrick Abercrombie identified Wythenshawe as the only undeveloped land suitable for building a housing estate close to Manchester To turn his proposal into a reality, Ernest and Shena Simon bought Wythenshawe Hall from Robert Henry Grenville Tatton in 1926, which they donated to the city's corporation (now known as the council) The idea was that people could be rehoused away from industrial Manchester into what became known as the "Garden City" To celebrate 100 years, BBC North West Tonight has spoken to 100 people from the area about what Wythenshawe means to them

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Wythenshawe 100: Cabaret club on Europe's biggest council estate - BBC News Image source, John Orchard Image caption, The Golden Garter in Wythenshawe proved to be a popular venue when it opened in 1968 By Kaya Black and Lauren Hirst , North West Published 1 hour ago When the Golden Garter cabaret club opened its doors for the first time in October 1968, TV legend Sir Bruce Forsyth was the first name on the door. Situated on a council estate in the Wythenshawe area of Manchester, people travelled from far and wide to enjoy shows at the 1,400-capacity venue. From music stars Dusty Springfield, Roy Orbison and Eartha Kitt to comedians Tommy Cooper and Ronnie Corbett, there was never a shortage of acts wanting to appear. "I think Dusty Springfield was the big highlight for me," said 79-year-old John Orchard, who was a pianist for Shep's Banjo Boys from 1969 to 1972. "She was my favourite singer in the 1960s and all of a sudden there she is at the Golden Garter. "This is a nightclub in Wythenshawe under the flight path of the Ringway airport (now known as Manchester Airport) in the middle of the biggest council estate in Europe. "So it was a bit incongruous, but it was a fantastic place and Wythenshawe loved it and it loved Wythenshawe." Image source, Unknown Image caption, The Golden Garter could pack in crowds of up to 1,400 The Golden Garter holds many happy memories for Paul Stoloff, who was a bassist for the Golden Garter Showband from 1970 to 1982. "It was good fun - happy times," he said. "It was interesting because it was different music every week. "So if you didn't like what they're doing, it'd be different for the next week." title: Motorcyclist killed by vehicle on M56 after police pursuit

evidence_packet.title: Motorcyclist killed by vehicle on M56 after police pursuit
evidence_packet.lead: The man was spotted driving dangerously by officers on the M60 near Stockport Pyramid, police say
evidence_packet.summary: The man was spotted driving dangerously by officers on the M60 near Stockport Pyramid, police say
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Motorcyclist killed by vehicle on M56 after police pursuit - BBC News Image source, Press Association Image caption, Greater Manchester Police is appealing for information Published 18 October 2026 A motorcycle rider being pursued by police on a motorway has been killed after he fled his bike and was hit by another vehicle. Officers spotted a red motorcycle being driven in a dangerous manner on the M60 clockwise around Stockport Pyramid shortly before 19:30 BST on Saturday, Greater Manchester Police (GMP) said. The force said it was brought to a stop on the M56 but the man ran off across the motorway and was hit and killed by another vehicle. GMP said, in line with procedures following a fatality after police contact, it has referred the matter to the Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC). The motorcycle had been posing a significant risk to members of the public using the motorway, the force said. "Tactical contact" was made with the bike at low speed on the hard shoulder by junction 5 near Manchester Airport and it was brought to a stop between junctions 3 and 4 of the M56 near Wythenshawe, it said. The rider was given emergency medical treatment by an ambulance crew but he was pronounced dead at the scene. A second man, who was not involved in the initial pursuit, was arrested at the scene on suspicion of causing death by careless driving when under the influence of drink or drugs and causing death by driving uninsured. The incident resulted in the closure of part of the M56 overnight. GMP has referred the matter to the IOPC which has decided an independent investigation is required. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Hindley couple spent 20 years building railway station garden - BBC News Image caption, The community garden has been created beside both platforms at Hindley station in Wigan By Richard Stead North West Published 18 October 2026 A couple who have spent 20 years building a community garden at their local railway station have said they hope it will be named as the Best in Britain. Hindley Station in Wigan has been nominated in an annual "World Cup" of stations competition run by train operating companies. Sheila and Sandy Davidson have been planting trees, flowers and shrubs alongside the platforms for two decades. "We just came down almost 20 years ago and decided to plant a few bulbs on the Manchester-bound platform," said 80-year-old Sheila from the Friends of Hindley Station. "Everybody in the area is wonderful, they all support us and we get so much help from people on social media who donate things for the garden." Image caption, Sheila Davidson is the Friends of Hindley Station's lead volunteer Sheila added: "It's putting Hindley on the map, so to even get in the World Cup of stations is such an honour, but we really would like to win." The Rail Delivery Group, which represents train operating companies, organises the competition every year, with passengers voting for the winner. Ashington railway station in Northumberland won the award last year after passenger services returned to the town in 2024 following an absence of 60 years. Image caption, The platforms at Hindley Station have been turned into vibrant community gardens and allotments Hindley station opened in 1848 and is situated between Bolton and Wigan, with regular direct services across the north of England. evidence_packet.summary: The two primary schools in Stockport and Dukinfield are both placed in special measures
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Greater Manchester schools told to urgently improve by inspectors - BBC News Image source, Press Association Image caption, Ofsted has changed its rating system By Charlotte Hall Local Democracy Reporting Service Published 18 October 2026 Two schools in Greater Manchester have been told they need urgent improvement following Ofsted inspections. St Thomas' Church of England Primary in Stockport has been placed in special measures with inspectors raising concerns about teaching, attendance and leadership. Ravensfield Primary in Dukinfield, already in special measures after staff reported violence towards teachers had reached "untenable levels", had only made minor improvements, inspectors said. The CLIC Trust, which runs Ravensfield, said management "recognised the seriousness of Ofsted's findings" and were committed to "delivering rapid improvements". St Thomas' Primary School has been contacted for comment. The government watchdog found the Stockport school was "failing to provide an acceptable standard of education". It was criticised for leaving pupils "ill-equipped" for the next stage of their education, with a "patchy" knowledge of most subjects. According to the report, too many children were also persistently absent, the Local Democracy Reporting Service , external said. Lead inspector David Spruce found pupils had been "hindered by a range of factors that ultimately stem from ineffective leadership and governance". evidence_packet.title: What does Wythenshawe mean to the people who know it best?
evidence_packet.lead: This year marks 100 years since Wythenshawe Hall was donated to Manchester Corporation At the time, the city was in urgent need of more housing In 1920 an urban planner called Patrick Abercrombie identified Wythenshawe as the only undeveloped land suitable for building a housing
evidence_packet.summary: This year marks 100 years since Wythenshawe Hall was donated to Manchester Corporation At the time, the city was in urgent need of more housing In 1920 an urban planner called Patrick Abercrombie identified Wythenshawe as the only undeveloped land suitable for building a housing
evidence_packet.evidence_text: This year marks 100 years since Wythenshawe Hall was donated to Manchester Corporation At the time, the city was in urgent need of more housing In 1920 an urban planner called Patrick Abercrombie identified Wythenshawe as the only undeveloped land suitable for building a housing estate close to Manchester To turn his proposal into a reality, Ernest and Shena Simon bought Wythenshawe Hall from Robert Henry Grenville Tatton in 1926, which they donated to the city's corporation (now known as the council) The idea was that people could be rehoused away from industrial Manchester into what became known as the "Garden City" To celebrate 100 years, BBC North West Tonight has spoken to 100 people from the area about what Wythenshawe means to them

evidence_packet.summary: After struggling to find a network for black entrepreneurs, a Manchester-based businessman said he decided to start his own David Chipfupa moved from Berkshire four years ago for a change of lifestyle But the 37-year-old said working remotely in technology sales soon left him fee
evidence_packet.evidence_text: After struggling to find a network for black entrepreneurs, a Manchester-based businessman said he decided to start his own David Chipfupa moved from Berkshire four years ago for a change of lifestyle But the 37-year-old said working remotely in technology sales soon left him feeling professionally isolated "I didn't really see a space where black professionals could network," he said. "There were events but there wasn't really a community in Manchester. Now our community is a celebration of black success and black excellence every day." Since Chipfupa founded Afrosocial in 2024 the network now has more than 4,000 members and has reached Australia, Dubai, South Africa and the United States "I wasn't going to the office and it was isolating," David told the BBC

evidence_packet.evidence_text: When the Golden Garter cabaret club opened its doors for the first time in October 1968, TV legend Sir Bruce Forsyth was the first name on the door Situated on a council estate in the Wythenshawe area of Manchester, people travelled from far and wide to enjoy shows at the 1,400-capacity venue From music stars Dusty Springfield, Roy Orbison and Eartha Kitt to comedians Tommy Cooper and Ronnie Corbett, there was never a shortage of acts wanting to appear "I think Dusty Springfield was the big highlight for me," said 79-year-old John Orchard, who was a pianist for Shep's Banjo Boys from 1969 to 1972 "She was my favourite singer in the 1960s and all of a sudden there she is at the Golden Garter "This is a nightclub in Wythenshawe under the flight path of the Ringway airport (now known as Manchester Airport) in the middle of the biggest council estate in Europe

title: Motorcyclist killed by vehicle on M56 after police pursuit

evidence_packet.title: Motorcyclist killed by vehicle on M56 after police pursuit
evidence_packet.lead: A motorcycle rider being pursued by police on a motorway has been killed after he fled his bike and was hit by another vehicle Officers spotted a red motorcycle being driven in a dangerous manner on the M60 clockwise around Stockport Pyramid shortly before 19:30 BST on Saturday
evidence_packet.summary: A motorcycle rider being pursued by police on a motorway has been killed after he fled his bike and was hit by another vehicle Officers spotted a red motorcycle being driven in a dangerous manner on the M60 clockwise around Stockport Pyramid shortly before 19:30 BST on Saturday
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A motorcycle rider being pursued by police on a motorway has been killed after he fled his bike and was hit by another vehicle Officers spotted a red motorcycle being driven in a dangerous manner on the M60 clockwise around Stockport Pyramid shortly before 19:30 BST on Saturday, Greater Manchester Police (GMP) said The force said it was brought to a stop on the M56 but the man ran off across the motorway and was hit and killed by another vehicle GMP said, in line with procedures following a fatality after police contact, it has referred the matter to the Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) The motorcycle had been posing a significant risk to members of the public using the motorway, the force said "Tactical contact" was made with the bike at low speed on the hard shoulder by junction 5 near Manchester Airport and it was brought to a stop between junctions 3 and 4 of the M56 near Wythenshawe, it said

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Politics From next month, these two Greater Manchester councils could be acting unlawfully Government planning reforms come into effect on October 31. But the two Greater Manchester councils voted not to accept them Add to preferred sources Comments N Two Greater Manchester planning departments will be acting unlawfully in less than two weeks after rejecting government changes to the way planning applications are approved and denied Councillors in both Tameside and Bolton voted not to accept new measures to implement legally binding changes, which means as things stand, from November 1 their planning committees will not be legally compliant and councillors will have no say on planning matters After that date, if nothing changes, officers will make all planning decisions in the two boroughs, it is understood. However, as the situation is unprecedented the true ramifications of not accepting the new reforms is unknown At recent full council meetings, councillors in Tameside and Bolton were told of the statutory introduction of the national scheme of delegation of planning functions will come into law on October 31, which alters arrangements for determining planning applications across England Under the new rules planning applications would be split into two tiers – Schedule 1 applications and Schedule 2 applications, designated by planning officers. Schedule 1 includes smaller and more technical applications that would only be dealt with by planning officers

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Metrolink Three Metrolink lines will close for two weeks from tomorrow Passengers are being warned of disruption Add to preferred sources News Damon Wilkinson Reporter 11:50, 18 Oct 2026 View Image Work to replace tracks along a 4km stretch arounsd Tr Three Metrolink lines are to close for fortnight from tomorrow (Monday) for engineering works on one of the busiest stretches of tram line in Europe. Deansgate-Castlefield, Cornbrook and Trafford Bar stations will shut until Monday, November 2, Transport for Greater Manchester (T The two-week closure will mean there will be no trams running on the Altrincham , Trafford Centre and Eccles lines. Meanwhile the station closures will also mean services to East Didsbury and Manchester Airport will end at Firswood, while the Rochdale line will stop at Exchange S The impacted stretch is ‘one of the busiest in Europe’ with trams passing through every 30 seconds for 20 hours a day, seven days a week. TfGM said the work will allow further speed restrictions along the line to be lifted, making journeys ‘quicker and more reliable’ Match-going United and City fans are also being warned the closures could affect them. City are due to host AEK Athens in the Champions League on Tuesday, Brighton in the Carabao Cup on October 28, and the same opponents in the Premier League on October 31 Meanwhile, United will take on Bournemouth at Old Trafford on October 25 in the Premier League. The works will see around 4km of track replaced as part of a wider £150m project

Flight U2415 departed Glasgow Airport at 8.25am on Sunday, October 18 bound for Southampton Airport The Airbus A319 was due to arrive on the South Coast at around 9.25am but was forced to divert to Liverpool John Lennon Airport after declaring an emergency around 25 minutes into the flight Data from flight tracking app FlightRadar24 shows the plane traveling south at around 24,000ft over Lancashire in north-west England when the emergency squawk code 7700 was issued It then circles in the skies above Liverpool as it descends to land in the city. The flight landed safely at shortly before 9.10am The reason for the emergency and the diversion is currently unknown. The flight departed around 20 minutes later than scheduled but was still due to arrive at Southampton on time, reports the Daily Record

The Royal Albert Edward Infirmary is to get improved same day emergency care facilities It is one of 14 new urgent care schemes across England being announced by the government today (October 18), with a total investment of almost £140 million. The new funding follows previous investment for the winter announced in April, at hospitals including Wigan Infirmary and S The government says the Wigan same day emergency care facilities will be moved closer to A&E. Meanwhile, new diagnostic services will help suitable patients access assessment and treatment more efficiently and return home the same day where appropriate, the government says Health and Social Care Secretary Yvette Cooper said: “Winter will be more challenging for our NHS this year, after such a heavy summer. Because, expense aside, it is all rather lovely But how did this dramatic transformation of a once-forgotten part of Manchester happen? And was it really for the good of the city, including those who cannot afford the £5.30 it costs for a loaf from Pollen or the rents around here that top £2,000 a month? The answer involves a remarkable cast of characters, from former Prime Minister David Cameron to Manchester City's Emirati owner, Sheikh Mansour, Sir Howard Bernstein, Sir Richard Leese and the new Prime Minister, Andy Burnham, who has made much during his ascent to the top job o It is a story of political manoeuvring in Downing Street, the search for soft power and global influence, and a long-term partnership between Manchester town hall and Abu Dhabi's “man in Manhattan”

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Politics From next month, these two Greater Manchester councils could be acting unlawfully Government planning reforms come into effect on October 31. But the two Greater Manchester councils voted not to accept them Add to preferred sources Comments N Two Greater Manchester planning departments will be acting unlawfully in less than two weeks after rejecting government changes to the way planning applications are approved and denied Councillors in both Tameside and Bolton voted not to accept new measures to implement legally binding changes, which means as things stand, from November 1 their planning committees will not be legally compliant and councillors will have no say on planning matters After that date, if nothing changes, officers will make all planning decisions in the two boroughs, it is understood. However, as the situation is unprecedented the true ramifications of not accepting the new reforms is unknown At recent full council meetings, councillors in Tameside and Bolton were told of the statutory introduction of the national scheme of delegation of planning functions will come into law on October 31, which alters arrangements for determining planning applications across England Under the new rules planning applications would be split into two tiers – Schedule 1 applications and Schedule 2 applications, designated by planning officers. Schedule 1 includes smaller and more technical applications that would only be dealt with by planning officers

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Metrolink Three Metrolink lines will close for two weeks from tomorrow Passengers are being warned of disruption Add to preferred sources News Damon Wilkinson Reporter 11:50, 18 Oct 2026 View Image Work to replace tracks along a 4km stretch arounsd Tr Three Metrolink lines are to close for fortnight from tomorrow (Monday) for engineering works on one of the busiest stretches of tram line in Europe. Deansgate-Castlefield, Cornbrook and Trafford Bar stations will shut until Monday, November 2, Transport for Greater Manchester (T The two-week closure will mean there will be no trams running on the Altrincham , Trafford Centre and Eccles lines. Meanwhile the station closures will also mean services to East Didsbury and Manchester Airport will end at Firswood, while the Rochdale line will stop at Exchange S The impacted stretch is ‘one of the busiest in Europe’ with trams passing through every 30 seconds for 20 hours a day, seven days a week. TfGM said the work will allow further speed restrictions along the line to be lifted, making journeys ‘quicker and more reliable’ Match-going United and City fans are also being warned the closures could affect them. City are due to host AEK Athens in the Champions League on Tuesday, Brighton in the Carabao Cup on October 28, and the same opponents in the Premier League on October 31 Meanwhile, United will take on Bournemouth at Old Trafford on October 25 in the Premier League. The works will see around 4km of track replaced as part of a wider £150m project

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Stretford Search launched for three missing boys last seen at Stretford Metrolink stop as police issue urgent appeal Police say they are growing incresingly concerned for Riley, Kian and Noah Add to preferred sources News Damon Wilkinson Reporter 09:2 Police are searching for three boys who went missing last night (Saturday). The youngsters, aged 12 and 13, were last seen at Stretford Metrolink stop at 6.50pm Police have appealed for the public's help in finding them. Officers say they are 'becoming increasingly concerned' about all three and want to make sure they are 'safe and well' It's not known if the boys - Riley, Noah and Kian - are together. Riley, 13, is described as 4ft 9ins, of slim build, with freckles and blonde curly hair. He was last wearing a black Adidas tracksuit top, a green North Face coat, and black Adidas tracksuit bottoms Noah, 12, was last wearing a black tracksuit, black T-shirt, black sweatshirt, and a black jacket with Reebok on the back. Kian, 12, is described as a white male, 5ft 5lins, of slim build, with blonde hair He was last wearing a black tracksuit, black trainers, and a purple T-shirt

evidence_packet.evidence_text: National news easyJet flight 'declares mid-air emergency' and diverts to Liverpool The flight declared the emergency squawk code 7700 Add to preferred sources Comments News Stephen Bark and Paul Britton Reporter 11:03, 18 Oct 2026 View Image easyJet ( An easyJet flight from Glasgow has diverted to Liverpool after declaring a mid-air emergency. Flight U2415 departed Glasgow Airport at 8.25am on Sunday, October 18 bound for Southampton Airport The Airbus A319 was due to arrive on the South Coast at around 9.25am but was forced to divert to Liverpool John Lennon Airport after declaring an emergency around 25 minutes into the flight Data from flight tracking app FlightRadar24 shows the plane traveling south at around 24,000ft over Lancashire in north-west England when the emergency squawk code 7700 was issued It then circles in the skies above Liverpool as it descends to land in the city. The flight landed safely at shortly before 9.10am The reason for the emergency and the diversion is currently unknown. The flight departed around 20 minutes later than scheduled but was still due to arrive at Southampton on time, reports the Daily Record

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Health Greater Manchester care service makes ‘significant’ improvements but still has more to do, weekly healthcare inspections reveal Services in Bolton, Bury, Rochdale, Salford, Stockport, Tameside and Trafford all received ratings this week Add to A Greater Manchester care service has made ‘significant’ improvements since its last inspection but has more work to do, the latest healthcare inspection round-up reveals Premier Care Limited Specialised Services, in Stretford , received this week's only negative rating from the Care Quality Commission (CQC). It was judged as ‘requires improvement’ by the watchdog, which raised concerns over medicine safety and leadership The supported living and homecare agency received good ratings for caring, effectiveness and responsiveness, however, and inspectors judged that improvements had been made since their 2025 visit, noting a ‘significant difference’ The service said it is ‘committed to continually strengthening this service, ensuring that every individual we support receives the safe, respectful, and high-quality care they deserve’ Here is a breakdown of Greater Manchester’s recently published CQC reports

evidence_packet.lead: NHS Wigan Infirmary gets £4.7m boost as government announces more NHS winter funding It comes as the NHS gears up for a tough winter following a record-breaking summer Add to preferred sources News Stephen Topping Senior reporter 10:02, 18 Oct 2026 Vi A new £4.7 million urgent ca
evidence_packet.summary: NHS Wigan Infirmary gets £4.7m boost as government announces more NHS winter funding It comes as the NHS gears up for a tough winter following a record-breaking summer Add to preferred sources News Stephen Topping Senior reporter 10:02, 18 Oct 2026 Vi A new £4.7 million urgent ca
evidence_packet.evidence_text: NHS Wigan Infirmary gets £4.7m boost as government announces more NHS winter funding It comes as the NHS gears up for a tough winter following a record-breaking summer Add to preferred sources News Stephen Topping Senior reporter 10:02, 18 Oct 2026 Vi A new £4.7 million urgent care facility will be opened in Wigan - as the NHS prepares for 'one of its most challenging winters' after the busiest summer in its history . The Royal Albert Edward Infirmary is to get improved same day emergency care facilities It is one of 14 new urgent care schemes across England being announced by the government today (October 18), with a total investment of almost £140 million. The new funding follows previous investment for the winter announced in April, at hospitals including Wigan Infirmary and S The government says the Wigan same day emergency care facilities will be moved closer to A&E. Meanwhile, new diagnostic services will help suitable patients access assessment and treatment more efficiently and return home the same day where appropriate, the government says Health and Social Care Secretary Yvette Cooper said: “Winter will be more challenging for our NHS this year, after such a heavy summer. That’s why we have been preparing early and investing in extra urgent care capacity to help get patients the care they need “NHS staff worked incredibly hard to keep on top of the extra pressure this summer. Now we need to support them in delivering for patients through the winter season, so our NHS is there for all of us when we need it.”

The reason why that piece of news would be considered 'devastating' should be crystal clear Yet hundreds of social media profiles responded to the news with laughter last week. Dozens of accounts left comments celebrating it, to various levels of glee With the story being described as 'devastating' on the Manchester Evening News' Facebook page , Ursula Longworth replied: "Depends on how you look at it." Andy Taylor wrote: "Every cloud has a silver lining." "Great news," said Jean Morrell, Nic Lecher, Luke Alan and Kaze Sukimo. "Every little helps," wrote both Andrew Booth and Joe Dilks. John Murrow commented: "Oh well never mind." Marcus Arrowsmith asked: "Can someone explain why this is devastating?" Tracey Earp chimed in: "In other news it's my day off so off to pub."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Politics Inside Salford's 'HMO' problem A spree of vandalism has shaken neighbourhoods across Salford. But why has the city become the flashpoint of the 'HMO debate'? Charlotte Hall reports View 15 Images "We want to get out of here" (Image: Getty Ima Add to preferred sources News Charlotte Hall Local Democracy Reporter 07:07, 18 Oct 2026 Updated 10:03, 18 Oct 2026 The curtain twitches in the window of a smashed-up house covered in black graffiti. It reads: ‘NO HMOS, NO, NO’. A second later, a little face appears in the glass The youngster, aged four, and his two-year-old brother were luckily asleep upstairs when a gang of delinquents attacked their family home in Little Hulton. They hurled a brick through the living room window on Tuesday, October 13 But the dad, who didn’t wish to be named, was in the room reading a book. He’s been left visibly shaken “We want to get out of here,” he said. “It feels unsafe. We’ve lived here for a year and had no issues, until now “The police say they’re targeting HMOs, but this isn’t a HMO. It’s me and my wife, we have two small kids.”

Armed police were seen surrounding the shopping centre on Saturday afternoon (October 17) Greater Manchester Police says it was called out to a stabbing on the ninth level of the multi-storey car park at around 3.15pm. Emergency services found the boy, aged 14, with serious injuries consistent with a stab wound His injuries are not believed to be life-threatening or life-changing. It is believed 14-year-old boy victim was involved in an argument with other unknown males prior to being stabbed The Manchester Evening News understands the altercation occurred moments after a 'shoplifting incident' in the Arndale Centre. Several sources at the Arndale have reported the same timeline of events It's believed that more than one person was hurt during the incident, although this has not been confirmed by Greater Manchester Police. No arrests have been made in connection with the stabbing so far and enquiries remain ongoing

Because, expense aside, it is all rather lovely But how did this dramatic transformation of a once-forgotten part of Manchester happen? And was it really for the good of the city, including those who cannot afford the £5.30 it costs for a loaf from Pollen or the rents around here that top £2,000 a month? The answer involves a remarkable cast of characters, from former Prime Minister David Cameron to Manchester City's Emirati owner, Sheikh Mansour, Sir Howard Bernstein, Sir Richard Leese and the new Prime Minister, Andy Burnham, who has made much during his ascent to the top job o It is a story of political manoeuvring in Downing Street, the search for soft power and global influence, and a long-term partnership between Manchester town hall and Abu Dhabi's “man in Manhattan”

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Politics From next month, these two Greater Manchester councils could be acting unlawfully Government planning reforms come into effect on October 31. But the two Greater Manchester councils voted not to accept them Add to preferred sources Comments N Two Greater Manchester planning departments will be acting unlawfully in less than two weeks after rejecting government changes to the way planning applications are approved and denied Councillors in both Tameside and Bolton voted not to accept new measures to implement legally binding changes, which means as things stand, from November 1 their planning committees will not be legally compliant and councillors will have no say on planning matters After that date, if nothing changes, officers will make all planning decisions in the two boroughs, it is understood. However, as the situation is unprecedented the true ramifications of not accepting the new reforms is unknown At recent full council meetings, councillors in Tameside and Bolton were told of the statutory introduction of the national scheme of delegation of planning functions will come into law on October 31, which alters arrangements for determining planning applications across England Under the new rules planning applications would be split into two tiers – Schedule 1 applications and Schedule 2 applications, designated by planning officers. Schedule 1 includes smaller and more technical applications that would only be dealt with by planning officers

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Metrolink Three Metrolink lines will close for two weeks from tomorrow Passengers are being warned of disruption Add to preferred sources News Damon Wilkinson Reporter 11:50, 18 Oct 2026 View Image Work to replace tracks along a 4km stretch arounsd Tr Three Metrolink lines are to close for fortnight from tomorrow (Monday) for engineering works on one of the busiest stretches of tram line in Europe. Deansgate-Castlefield, Cornbrook and Trafford Bar stations will shut until Monday, November 2, Transport for Greater Manchester (T The two-week closure will mean there will be no trams running on the Altrincham , Trafford Centre and Eccles lines. Meanwhile the station closures will also mean services to East Didsbury and Manchester Airport will end at Firswood, while the Rochdale line will stop at Exchange S The impacted stretch is ‘one of the busiest in Europe’ with trams passing through every 30 seconds for 20 hours a day, seven days a week. TfGM said the work will allow further speed restrictions along the line to be lifted, making journeys ‘quicker and more reliable’ Match-going United and City fans are also being warned the closures could affect them. City are due to host AEK Athens in the Champions League on Tuesday, Brighton in the Carabao Cup on October 28, and the same opponents in the Premier League on October 31 Meanwhile, United will take on Bournemouth at Old Trafford on October 25 in the Premier League. The works will see around 4km of track replaced as part of a wider £150m project

evidence_packet.evidence_text: National news easyJet flight 'declares mid-air emergency' and diverts to Liverpool The flight declared the emergency squawk code 7700 Add to preferred sources Comments News Stephen Bark and Paul Britton Reporter 11:03, 18 Oct 2026 View Image easyJet ( An easyJet flight from Glasgow has diverted to Liverpool after declaring a mid-air emergency. Flight U2415 departed Glasgow Airport at 8.25am on Sunday, October 18 bound for Southampton Airport The Airbus A319 was due to arrive on the South Coast at around 9.25am but was forced to divert to Liverpool John Lennon Airport after declaring an emergency around 25 minutes into the flight Data from flight tracking app FlightRadar24 shows the plane traveling south at around 24,000ft over Lancashire in north-west England when the emergency squawk code 7700 was issued It then circles in the skies above Liverpool as it descends to land in the city. The flight landed safely at shortly before 9.10am The reason for the emergency and the diversion is currently unknown. The flight departed around 20 minutes later than scheduled but was still due to arrive at Southampton on time, reports the Daily Record

evidence_packet.summary: Politics Inside Salford's 'HMO' problem A spree of vandalism has shaken neighbourhoods across Salford. But why has the city become the flashpoint of the 'HMO debate'?
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Politics Inside Salford's 'HMO' problem A spree of vandalism has shaken neighbourhoods across Salford. But why has the city become the flashpoint of the 'HMO debate'? Charlotte Hall reports View 15 Images "We want to get out of here" (Image: Getty Ima Add to preferred sources News Charlotte Hall Local Democracy Reporter 07:07, 18 Oct 2026 Updated 10:03, 18 Oct 2026 The curtain twitches in the window of a smashed-up house covered in black graffiti. It reads: ‘NO HMOS, NO, NO’. A second later, a little face appears in the glass The youngster, aged four, and his two-year-old brother were luckily asleep upstairs when a gang of delinquents attacked their family home in Little Hulton. They hurled a brick through the living room window on Tuesday, October 13 But the dad, who didn’t wish to be named, was in the room reading a book. He’s been left visibly shaken “We want to get out of here,” he said. “It feels unsafe. We’ve lived here for a year and had no issues, until now “The police say they’re targeting HMOs, but this isn’t a HMO. It’s me and my wife, we have two small kids.”

GIA and IGI document lab-grown diamonds differently, and an older report may not look like a current one. Understanding the format helps you judge what is actually being of GIA, the Gemological Institute of America, and IGI, the International Gemological Institute, are grading laboratories. Retailers often refer to these documents as diamond certificates. Check the issuing laboratory and the details on the report itself The lab diamonds UK shoppers compare may have reports from different laboratories. Lily Arkwright, which has a showroom in Didsbury, lists lab-grown diamond rings with GIA or IGI documentation. Ask to see your shortlisted stone’s report before visiting, so you can discuss its det Start by checking the laboratory’s name, the report number and whether the document identifies the diamond as laboratory-grown. Establish which stone it describes, especially if the ring also contains smaller accent diamonds GIA introduced its Laboratory-Grown Diamond Quality Assessment on the 1st of October 2025. title: Motorcyclist killed by vehicle on M56 after police pursuit

evidence_packet.title: Motorcyclist killed by vehicle on M56 after police pursuit
evidence_packet.lead: Officers spotted a red motorcycle being driven in a dangerous manner on the M60 clockwise around Stockport Pyramid shortly before 19:30 BST on Saturday, Greater Manchester Police (GMP) said The force said it was brought to a stop on the M56 but the man ran off across the motorway
evidence_packet.summary: Officers spotted a red motorcycle being driven in a dangerous manner on the M60 clockwise around Stockport Pyramid shortly before 19:30 BST on Saturday, Greater Manchester Police (GMP) said The force said it was brought to a stop on the M56 but the man ran off across the motorway
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Officers spotted a red motorcycle being driven in a dangerous manner on the M60 clockwise around Stockport Pyramid shortly before 19:30 BST on Saturday, Greater Manchester Police (GMP) said The force said it was brought to a stop on the M56 but the man ran off across the motorway and was hit and killed by another vehicle GMP said, in line with procedures following a fatality after police contact, it has referred the matter to the Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) The motorcycle had been posing a significant risk to members of the public using the motorway, the force said "Tactical contact" was made with the bike at low speed on the hard shoulder by junction 5 near Manchester Airport and it was brought to a stop between junctions 3 and 4 of the M56 near Wythenshawe, it said The rider was given emergency medical treatment by an ambulance crew but he was pronounced dead at the scene

evidence_packet.title: Alisha Samuels murder: Man no longer suspect, police say
evidence_packet.lead: Alisha Samuels, 26, was pronounced dead at the scene after officers were called to reports of a disturbance on Dorking Avenue in Newton Heath at about 02:00 BST on Thursday Greater Manchester Police said the 25-year-old man had been released on police bail pending further inquiri
evidence_packet.summary: Alisha Samuels, 26, was pronounced dead at the scene after officers were called to reports of a disturbance on Dorking Avenue in Newton Heath at about 02:00 BST on Thursday Greater Manchester Police said the 25-year-old man had been released on police bail pending further inquiri
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Alisha Samuels, 26, was pronounced dead at the scene after officers were called to reports of a disturbance on Dorking Avenue in Newton Heath at about 02:00 BST on Thursday Greater Manchester Police said the 25-year-old man had been released on police bail pending further inquiries into other matters Detectives said their investigation remained active and that they were continuing to seek other people believed to have been involved in the incident Det Chief Insp Justin Bryant, the senior investigating officer, said: "While a man has been released on police bail as our enquiries continue, our investigation remains very much active "We are relentlessly pursuing those responsible for Alisha's death and are continuing to seek those outstanding individuals believed to have been involved in this incident." Det Chief Insp Justin Bryant urged people not to speculate about the circumstances of Ms Samuels' death, saying misinformation could hinder the investigation and cause further distress to her family

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Oldham Council has secured a court order requiring the removal of an unauthorised encampment from Oldham Edge Council officers first visited the site on Thursday 6th August following concerns from residents and people using the park. Officers spoke to those at the encampment, who said they intended to leave by Saturday 8th August As the site had not been vacated, the Council returned with support from Greater Manchester Police on Tuesday 11th August. A formal direction was served under Section 77 of the Criminal Justice and Public Order Act 1994, requiring those at the encampment to leave and remove their The Council also provided information about authorised sites in Greater Manchester, along with advice about health, wellbeing and reporting hate crime After the direction was not followed, the Council began court proceedings. This update explains the current position, what survey activity means and how local people can take part in any future planning process In August 2026, Wigan Council’s Cabinet agreed to object to Peel Land’s proposed Gibfield Park masterplan. Cabinet’s position was that the housing and industrial proposals were not acceptable in their current form and did not have cabinet members’ support. No planning application West of Gibfield was allocated for homes, employment and green space through Places for Everyone, which was adopted in 2024 and now forms part of the statutory development plan. The current Wigan Local Plan process cannot reverse that allocation. However, allocation does not gran Our chief executive has written to the Greater Manchester Combined Authority, requesting Gibfield to be removed from the plan. We are waiting for a response Cabinet has formally objected to the proposed masterplan and made clear that it cannot support the development now or in the future Peel Land may undertake ecology surveys, ground-condition testing, environmental work and traffic or transport studies to understand the site and prepare evidence. These investigations do not mean planning permission has been granted or that a future application will be approved

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

From a childhood in exile to surviving secret detention in China, his remarkable life and career have led him to global prominence. Using sculpture, installation, film, photography In Button Up! , the artist turns his lens on two centuries of Chinese and British relations. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians. Beat the Jams live series showcases the very best of the jazz scene, at short rush hour gigs from 6pm at Band on the Wall. What better way to avoid those endless queues, chaotic traffic and stressful homeward journeys? Clock off and skip the rush-hour traffic while you watch live jazz and make the most of our happy hour deals from 5–7pm: £4.50 pints / 2 for £15 cocktails / £15 bottles of wine + pizzas from £5! The new season kicks off on 24 September with tenor saxophonist Dean Masser and pianist Richard Wetherall, followed by: 7 October – Anna Chandler-King Quartet Leeds based saxophonist and composer Anna joins us again for Beat the Jams, this time with her own band. Anna’s thoughtful and inventive compositions are firm favourites of us at Beat the Jams and her quartet promises to be a unique rush hour busting treat! 16 November – Sam Lightwing Quartet Saxophonist and composer Sam Lightwing brings presents brand new music for his thrilling young quartet, showcasing Sam’s original compositions, which blend classic mainstream jazz grooves with modern flavours of post-pop and latin, all wrapped up in the language of contemporary sax giants such as Chris Potter, Seamus Blake and Joshua Redman. 15 December – Svarc/Devine/Walsh with Richard Iles The band combines deep pocket, fearless interplay and a shared love of exploration. Expect everything from soulful melodies and infectious rhythms to moments of exhilarating collective improvisation, delivered with the chemistry that only world-class musicians can create. Tickets from £13 per show, or £42 for a season ticket

evidence_packet.evidence_text: The Olllam is a band that fuses Irish traditional music with the modern jazz/post-rock energy of Detroit. He also confirmed that AI will be a central focus of the That felt particularly relevant following an event we hosted through the UK Tech Cluster Group with AI Minister Kanishka Narayan, North East Mayor Kim McGuinness and other regional leaders, looking at AI, devolution and local growth One of the clearest themes from the discussion was that devolution should not mean every place trying to build the same thing. Different regions have different strengths, assets and specialisms, and there was a strong view that greater collaboration between places could create bi Procurement and buying local also featured strongly. The discussion highlighted the role public sector buying power can play in supporting regional businesses, helping successful pilots move into commercial contracts and strengthening UK capability in areas such as AI and cyber There was also a broader conversation about sovereignty and the UK’s role internationally. title: Is the funding market getting harder and what could that mean for Manchester? | Manchester Digital

evidence_packet.title: Is the funding market getting harder and what could that mean for Manchester? | Manchester Digital
evidence_packet.lead: Tech investment isn't slowing down, but the pattern of investment is changing.
evidence_packet.summary: Tech investment isn't slowing down, but the pattern of investment is changing. As investors grow increasingly selective, the capital ecosystem has become polarised
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Tech investment isn't slowing down, but the pattern of investment is changing. As investors grow increasingly selective, the capital ecosystem has become polarised. More capital is being concentrated in fewer companies while the market for exits remains difficult Financial news recently added another dimension to that discussion. AI-related shares fell last week after Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called for a slower approach to the development of increasingly capable AI models. Nvidia finished the day down 3.4%, SoftBank fell 10.7% in Tokyo Additionally, the Bank of England is predicted to increase interest rates later this year, which could affect the North West's tech funding landscape by raising the cost of capital across the board, compressing valuations, pushing investors toward profitability over growth-at-all The British Business Bank's 2026 Small Business Equity Tracker found that equity investment into UK smaller businesses fell 4% to £12.3bn in 2025. Seed deal numbers fell 27% and venture deals fell 13%. AI companies attracted 44% of all investment into smaller businesses while the Beauhurst recorded £14.4bn of UK equity investment across 2,799 deals in the first half of 2026 but three AI companies accounted for 29% of all the capital raised. Those very large rounds can make the overall market look stronger than it feels to businesses raising at seed or Ser Beauhurst's analysis shows that UK equity investment more than doubled between 2017 and 2021 to £32.2bn while annual exits remained at around 400 to 500. An exit takes a median of four years from a funding round

evidence_packet.evidence_text: In 1965, The Sunday Times Magazine sent photojournalist John Bulmer north to document the region at a time when it was defined by industrial decline. But the images he returned with told a more complex story: shot in colour, they showed humanity and dignity alongside the hardship Sixty years later, photographer Simon Hill has retraced that journey. The conversation between their two bodies of work, now showing together at Jodrell Bank, builds a portrait of how much has changed since then and how much remains While Bulmer visited 16 locations across the North, Hill travelled to more than 50. From late 2024 to mid 2026 he crossed the historic seven counties from Newcastle to Liverpool, visiting former mining communities, coastal towns, city centres, remote landscapes, and the motorways In homage to Bulmer’s pioneering use of colour, much of Hill’s work was shot on Harman Phoenix 200, a contemporary colour film made in the North, and known for its unpredictable, textured qualities Bulmer’s North captured communities facing uncertain futures as the industries that defined them began to disappear. Hill’s is post-industrial, more diverse and still evolving. Former centres of heavy industry have become sites of cultural reinvention and technological growth. Bu Jodrell Bank feels a particularly fitting setting for work that’s fundamentally about time, distance and how we measure change. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and t
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bolton Car Boot Sale is one of the North West's biggest weekly boot sales, held in the hardstanding car park of the Macron Stadium (formerly Reebok), Burnden Way, Horwich, Bolton BL6 6JW. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and thousands of bargain hunters each week. Sellers can arrive and set up from 6:00 AM, with buyers welcomed in from 7:00 AM. Entry costs just £1 per car for buyers. Pitches for sellers are £14 for a car, £20 for a van and £3 for a trailer, with regular and corner pitches available on request. Bring exact change to keep the queue moving, and call organiser Andrew on 07470784644 for more details. Expect hundreds of stalls across the concrete hardstanding pitches, so it goes ahead in most weather. On-site you'll find a 5-star catering service, doughnuts and coffee, ice cream and desserts, a meat auction, fresh fruit and veg, plants, and retro sweet stalls. The sale is dog-friendly, has male and female toilets, ample parking, and kids' rides and bouncy castles to keep little ones entertained. evidence_packet.evidence_text: 43 years on from our only participation in the European Cup – a first-round defeat to Fenerbahce in 1968 – we qualified for the Champions League for the 2011/12 season. Now, as we approach our 150th game in this historic competition when we take on AEK Athens on Tuesday, we can say the Champions League has more than delivered on its guarantee of joy, heartbreak and everything in between. Having qualified for the continent’s hallmark cup competition in every season since Roberto Mancini led us there in 2011, we are currently on the longest ongoing run of appearances in the Champions League of any English side. The level of consistency required not to miss out in all that time speaks volumes to our domestic dominance particularly under Pep Guardiola but also with Mancini and Manuel Pellegrini. We have, after all, won the Premier League more than every other club combined since that 2011/12 season began. However, it’s not always been the same in Europe. With the finest of margins often deciding knockout ties between the most talented players on the planet, it felt for a long time as if City were destined never to lift the famous old trophy with the giant ear-shaped handles. That all changed in 2023, when Rodri curled home against Inter in Istanbul and Ederson produced a last-minute diving save to set the seal on a historic Treble. City had more than deserved it, having swept aside German champions Bayern Munich and defending winners Real Madrid in the previous rounds. But what you deserve isn’t always what you get in the Champions League. Bernardo Silva, who left City in the summer as our joint-most decorated player having been integral to all the successes under Guardiola, said this in his final interview with the club: “I think more of our teams could have done the same.

title: Howard Webb reveals two Man United phone calls to 'acknowledge' major referee error

evidence_packet.title: Howard Webb reveals two Man United phone calls to 'acknowledge' major referee error
evidence_packet.lead: The head of referees has spoken about the decision to let Erling Haaland's goal stand during the Manchester Derby
evidence_packet.summary: The head of referees has spoken about the decision to let Erling Haaland's goal stand during the Manchester Derby
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Football Manchester United FC Howard Webb reveals two Man United phone calls to 'acknowledge' major referee error The head of referees has spoken about the decision to let Erling Haaland's goal stand during the Manchester Derby Add to preferred sources Comments Sport Amie W Referees chief Howard Webb has revealed that he made two phone calls to Manchester United in the aftermath of the Manchester Derby defeat. United fell to a 1-0 loss against rivals Man City , thanks to Erling Haaland ’s second half goal The goal was originally ruled out on the field, with VAR controversially overturning the decision despite Enzo Fernandez, who was offside, appearing to interfere with play. It’s a decision that Webb has described as a ‘significant error’ It was revealed after the game that Pro Ref had been in touch with United to admit an ‘error of judgement . Webb has now said that he personally made two phone calls to officials at the club Speaking to The Times , he said: “I called [director of football] Jason Wilcox and Rebecca [Britain, the club secretary], acknowledging the error “People talk about apologies. We don’t often apologise but I did that one because the error was so impactful — and it wasn’t a judgment call.”

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Football Manchester City injury news Haaland, Semenyo, Nunes - Man City injury news and return dates after Ipswich win Manchester City made it seven Premier League wins in a row on Saturday but ended the game sweating on the fitness of five players Add to preferred sources Manchester City beat Ipswich Town 3-2 on Saturday to extend their 100 per cent Premier League record to seven matches. Phil Foden ended his goal drought on 19 minutes when he converted Jeremy Doku's cross. Moments later The Tractor Boys were level through Daizen Maeda Erling Haaland's header put City back in front at half time. With just over 20 minutes to play, Haaland added his second to seemingly put the game to bed. The Norwegian thought he had completed his hat-trick with just a minute of normal time remaining, only for VAR to rule it out Incredibly, Ipswich broke up the other end and won a penalty, given after review, that Zian Flemming converted. The 12 added minutes ensured a nervy finale but City held on for the victory. While a positive result, it was not without negatives, particularly in regards to injuries Get all the best Man City news, updates and analysis straight to your Inbox courtesy of the MEN! City manager says ‘we need to make our noise’ Enzo Maresca has called on Manchester City fans to bring inflatable bananas to help inspire the team in their first Premier League home game since being found guilty of financial breaches when they tak Blow-up bananas became popular among City fans in the 1980s and 1990s when they spent time in the second and third tiers, and have been revived in reaction to the threat of being punished with relegation and to show there is plenty to reflect on before the 2008 takeover “Very nice,” Maresca said of the inflatables. “I didn’t know the history behind the banana.
